item.title: Over 250,000 evacuated as French, Spanish fires rage
item.description: Out-of-control wildfires raging in France and Spain have forced the evacuation of more than 250,000 people in total, authorities in both countries have said.

item.title: Woman dies, girl critical as car and truck crash in Cavan
item.description: A woman in her 50s has died and a child has been seriously injured following a collision between a car and a truck in Co Cavan yesterday.

item.title: Firefighters tackling blazes in Tipperary and Wicklow
item.description: Fire services personnel in Co Tipperary are tackling blazes at Slievenamon for a sixth day while in Co Wicklow the National Parks and Wildlife Service (NPWS) is continuing to assess the situation at a gorse fire in Glencree.

item.title: An AI agent went rogue - should we be worried?
item.description: OpenAI revealed this week that an AI agent went rogue and escaped during a security test. It sparked renewed calls for greater protections and guardrails for artificial intelligence.

item.title: Do tougher e-scooter laws work? What the evidence says
item.description: Several European countries have introduced e-scooter measures, researchers still have limited evidence showing which regulations are most effective at reducing harm

item.title: Houthis claim Saudi missile attack, US mulls Iran strikes
item.description: Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels have claimed a missile attack on Saudi Arabia, as US President Donald Trump mulled fresh strikes on Iran in the deepening Middle East war.

item.title: Our top 10 acts to see at All Together Now
item.description: With one week to go, we round up our top ten acts to see at All Together Now in Waterford . . .

item.title: Trump orders disclaimers outside American history museum
item.description: US President Donald Trump has issued an executive order to install signage that warns visitors of inaccurate historical information inside The Smithsonian's National Museum of American History in Washington.

item.title: Indian education minister resigns after mass protests
item.description: Indian Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan said he had resigned, handing a major victory to youth protesters nationwide who had demanded that he quit to take responsibility for examination paper leaks.

item.title: Officials linked Jordanian asylum rise to UK visa change
item.description: Department of Justice officials in Ireland linked a "marked increase" in Jordanian asylum seekers to British visa changes - months before the loophole was eventually closed, according to documents released to RTÉ News under Freedom of Information.

item.title: Who is the Russian oligarch behind Aughinish owner Rusal?
item.description: The founder of Rusal, the owner of Aughinish Alumina plant in Co Limerick, Oleg Deripaska, officially stood down as its leader seven years ago but remains a key figure in Russia's economy and politics.

item.title: Taoiseach brings message of 'strength with unity' to Kyiv
item.description: Support for Ukraine's EU ambitions and careful diplomacy over the Aughinish Alumina investigation summed up Taoiseach Micheál Martin's visit to the Ukrainian capital on Thursday this week.

item.title: Mayo continue to light the candle despite final horrors
item.description: Mayo's 11 All-Ireland final losses since their third triumph in 1951 have contained all sorts of misfortune possible. As they prepare to flip the script, here's how those deciders worked out.

item.title: Woman, 25, charged over bomb found in car in Co Monaghan
item.description: A 25-year-old woman has been charged in connection with the interception of a bomb that was discovered in a car in Carrickmacross in Co Monaghan on Wednesday.

item.title: Irish author shares terror of French wildfire ordeal
item.description: Author and food advocate Sophie Morris "woke to sirens, flames and a race to escape" after being caught up in a wildfire in southern France.

item.title: First financial literacy ambassadors appointed
item.description: The Government has announced the appointment of Ireland's first financial literacy ambassadors.

item.title: Do not cancel travel plans over fires - French minister
item.description: A French foreign minister has urged tourists not to cancel their travel plans despite unprecedented wildfires in the country's southwest.

item.title: Solid start key if energetic Mayo to threaten huge upset
item.description: If Kerry play to their best, they will have too much for Andy Moran's team at Mayo's current stage in development. But Kerry haven't found that gear this past two games, writes Enda McGinley

item.title: Flavio Bolsonaro to launch Brazil presidential candidacy
item.description: Battered by a string of political crises, Flavio Bolsonaro will today formally launch his candidacy for Brazil's October presidential election, seeking to follow in the footsteps of his father, Jair Bolsonaro.

item.title: Over 200,000 evacuated in Spanish and French wildfires
item.description: French authorities ordered the total evacuation of the Cap Ferret peninsula on the Atlantic Coast, sending boats to remove people from an area threatened by a major wildfire, while 40,000 people have been told to evacuate or shelter in the Madrid region.
